title: ISO 13485 QMS interface record
description: One thing MduX supplies to an integrating manufacturer's quality management system, and what that manufacturer must still do with it. This is deliberately not a schema for a quality management system: MduX is a software library and operates no QMS - no management review, no CAPA, no supplier qualification, no customers of its own. Modelling one here would be the same overclaim that retired docs/MduX_ISO-13485-Quality-Management-Framework.md (see docs/governance/superseded-documents.md). What a library does have is an interface: a small number of clauses where it produces something a manufacturer's QMS can consume as an input. Each record below is one such handover, and the manufacturer_obligation field is the part that keeps the record honest - every supplied artifact leaves work undone on the other side of the boundary.

clause_ref.description: The ISO 13485:2016 clause this record is about, in the citation-key format from docs/governance/citation-convention.md.

contribution_kind.description: What kind of QMS input this is. The closed set is short on purpose: these are the only three categories a library can genuinely produce. A clause needing anything else is a clause MduX does not contribute to, and the corpus says so in prose rather than inventing a record here.

supplied.description: Repository-relative paths to what MduX actually provides. Non-empty: a record with nothing behind it is a claim, not a contribution.

manufacturer_obligation.description: What the integrating manufacturer must still do for this clause to be satisfied for its device. Required, and required to be substantive: no MduX artifact discharges an ISO 13485 obligation on a manufacturer's behalf, so a record that left this blank would misrepresent the handover.

notes.description: Optional free text - a caveat, or a pointer to the module section that explains the mechanism.

examples.manufacturer_obligation: Decide whether the trust-zone boundary MduX enforces is the right boundary for this device, and record that decision in the device's own design history file. MduX verifies that governed code cannot reach Vulkan; it cannot know whether that is the separation this device's risk analysis requires.

Fold the baked artifacts and their reports into the device's own configuration record. ADR-007 fixes how an MduX artifact is derived and byte-verified; it says nothing about which artifacts this device ships or how long their records must be retained, both of which are device-level decisions.
